The deployment must be shut down before applying the new configuration.' and exit code 4 means the feature is disabled. However, this is a breaking change to the exit-code contract of the `update-compatibility check` command: any existing CI/CD pipeline or script written against the previous release (where 4 meant 'recreate upgrade required') will now misinterpret exit code 3 as an unexpected error (picocli software error is 1, usage error is 2, and scripts commonly treat any non-0/3/4 code as failure) and, worse, will treat exit code 4 as a distinct 'feature disabled' case only if they were updated. Since the tool is explicitly documented as 'fully scriptable' and 'GitOps friendly' with consumers relying on exit codes, silently renumbering an existing exit code (rather than only adding the new code 4) breaks backward compatibility for anyone already using the command. The renumbering should be avoided (keep RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4 and use a new code such as 5 for FEATURE_DISABLED), or at minimum the change must be called out as a breaking change in release notes; as written, the docs present the new numbering as if it were always the contract."

      "title": "Feature check runs before configuration validation, so --features=rolling-updates is never actually parsed for the check itself",

Profile.isFeatureEnabled reads the statically initialized Profile (Profile.getInstance()), which is only configured from CLI options/environment during the normal Keycloak configuration/validation phase. The `--features` option is a standard Keycloak CLI option processed by the configuration machinery; whether it has been applied to the Profile singleton at the point run() executes depends on command initialization order in the Quarkus CLI framework. The distribution test UpdateCommandDistTest passes `--features=rolling-updates` as a CLI argument and expects the command to proceed, which suggests the option is honored, but the ordering is fragile: if Profile is initialized lazily or the feature option is applied after run() begins (e.g., when running via `kc.sh update-compatibility ... --features=rolling-updates` in a non-optimized or build-affected mode), the check would incorrectly report the feature as disabled and exit 4 even though the user explicitly enabled it. The feature check should be performed after validateConfig() (which triggers full option processing) or the enabled-features state should be read from the parsed command options rather than the global Profile singleton, to make the gating deterministic."

The whole point of introducing CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 (and documenting it in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc lines 132-134 as the contract for scripts) is that automation can branch on exit code 4. Without an assertion such as `assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode())` (or the equivalent CLIResult API), a regression that exits with 0, 1, or 2 instead of 4 would not be caught, and the documented scripting contract would silently break.       "body": "In createInitialDeployment(UpdateStrategy updateStrategy), when updateStrategy is null the method returns early at line 105-107 (`if (updateStrategy == null) { return kc; }`) before the code at lines 112-115 that sets the FeatureSpec with Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(). The parameterized test upgradeStrategy() supplies both null and UpdateStrategy.RECREATE, so the null case (testImageChange-null and testCacheMaxCount-null) runs without the rolling-updates feature enabled in the Keycloak CR. Given that the operator documentation added in this PR (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc lines 446-450) states that 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail', the null-strategy test case is exercising a deployment configuration that the operator is documented to reject, and the test's expectations (e.g., eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus for testCacheMaxCount-null) may be passing for the wrong reason or masking a validation failure. Either the null case should also enable the feature (so both parameters test the strategy behavior with the feature on), or the test should explicitly assert the operator's behavior when the feature is missing. As written, the test coverage for the default (no update strategy) path does not match the documented requirement."
    },

      "file": "docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc",

      "severity": "low",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "Exit code table formatting is broken: rows 0-3 are missing the leading pipe, producing a malformed AsciiDoc table",
      "body": "In the exit-code table (lines 116-135), the first four rows begin with `m|0`, `m|1`, `m|2`, `m|3` while the newly added row begins with `m|4` — all are missing the leading `|` cell delimiter that AsciiDoc tables require (a cell must start with `|`). Only the header row `|===` / `|Exit Code |Description` and the final row use the correct `|` prefix. As a result the rendered table will be malformed: the `m|N` rows will not be parsed as table rows at all (the `m` is an unintended literal prefix), so exit codes 0 through 3 will render as plain paragraph text outside the table, and only the header and the new exit-code-4 row will appear as a table. The rows should be `m|0` corrected to `|0` (i.e., `|m|0` style consistent with the last row: a leading `|` followed by the `m` cell marker). This makes the documented exit-code contract — which scripts depend on — visually broken in the published guide."

findings.title: Exit code change from 4 to 3 for recreate upgrade breaks documented contract and existing automation
findings.body: The constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 in this PR. The accompanying documentation in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc (lines 128-130) is updated to say exit code 3 means 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The deployment must be shut down before applying the new configuration.' and exit code 4 means the feature is disabled. However, this is a breaking change to the exit-code contract of the `update-compatibility check` command: any existing CI/CD pipeline or script written against the previous release (where 4 meant 'recreate upgrade required') will now misinterpret exit code 3 as an unexpected error (picocli software error is 1, usage error is 2, and scripts commonly treat any non-0/3/4 code as failure) and, worse, will treat exit code 4 as a distinct 'feature disabled' case only if they were updated. Since the tool is explicitly documented as 'fully scriptable' and 'GitOps friendly' with consumers relying on exit codes, silently renumbering an existing exit code (rather than only adding the new code 4) breaks backward compatibility for anyone already using the command. The renumbering should be avoided (keep RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4 and use a new code such as 5 for FEATURE_DISABLED), or at minimum the change must be called out as a breaking change in release notes; as written, the docs present the new numbering as if it were always the contract.

findings.title: Feature check runs before configuration validation, so --features=rolling-updates is never actually parsed for the check itself
findings.body: In UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (and identically in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()), the guard `if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES))` is evaluated at the very start of run(), before `validateConfig()` is called. Profile.isFeatureEnabled reads the statically initialized Profile (Profile.getInstance()), which is only configured from CLI options/environment during the normal Keycloak configuration/validation phase. The `--features` option is a standard Keycloak CLI option processed by the configuration machinery; whether it has been applied to the Profile singleton at the point run() executes depends on command initialization order in the Quarkus CLI framework. The distribution test UpdateCommandDistTest passes `--features=rolling-updates` as a CLI argument and expects the command to proceed, which suggests the option is honored, but the ordering is fragile: if Profile is initialized lazily or the feature option is applied after run() begins (e.g., when running via `kc.sh update-compatibility ... --features=rolling-updates` in a non-optimized or build-affected mode), the check would incorrectly report the feature as disabled and exit 4 even though the user explicitly enabled it. The feature check should be performed after validateConfig() (which triggers full option processing) or the enabled-features state should be read from the parsed command options rather than the global Profile singleton, to make the gating deterministic.

findings.title: No test asserts the exit code for the feature-disabled path (exit code 4)
findings.body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled test only asserts that the error message 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled.' appears in the CLI output; it never asserts the process exit code. The whole point of introducing CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 (and documenting it in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc lines 132-134 as the contract for scripts) is that automation can branch on exit code 4. Without an assertion such as `assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode())` (or the equivalent CLIResult API), a regression that exits with 0, 1, or 2 instead of 4 would not be caught, and the documented scripting contract would silently break. The test should assert the exit code equals CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED.

findings.title: Test parameterization silently skips enabling the rolling-updates feature when updateStrategy is null
findings.body: In createInitialDeployment(UpdateStrategy updateStrategy), when updateStrategy is null the method returns early at line 105-107 (`if (updateStrategy == null) { return kc; }`) before the code at lines 112-115 that sets the FeatureSpec with Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(). The parameterized test upgradeStrategy() supplies both null and UpdateStrategy.RECREATE, so the null case (testImageChange-null and testCacheMaxCount-null) runs without the rolling-updates feature enabled in the Keycloak CR. Given that the operator documentation added in this PR (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc lines 446-450) states that 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail', the null-strategy test case is exercising a deployment configuration that the operator is documented to reject, and the test's expectations (e.g., eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus for testCacheMaxCount-null) may be passing for the wrong reason or masking a validation failure. Either the null case should also enable the feature (so both parameters test the strategy behavior with the feature on), or the test should explicitly assert the operator's behavior when the feature is missing. As written, the test coverage for the default (no update strategy) path does not match the documented requirement.

findings.title: Exit code table formatting is broken: rows 0-3 are missing the leading pipe, producing a malformed AsciiDoc table
findings.body: In the exit-code table (lines 116-135), the first four rows begin with `m|0`, `m|1`, `m|2`, `m|3` while the newly added row begins with `m|4` — all are missing the leading `|` cell delimiter that AsciiDoc tables require (a cell must start with `|`). Only the header row `|===` / `|Exit Code |Description` and the final row use the correct `|` prefix. As a result the rendered table will be malformed: the `m|N` rows will not be parsed as table rows at all (the `m` is an unintended literal prefix), so exit codes 0 through 3 will render as plain paragraph text outside the table, and only the header and the new exit-code-4 row will appear as a table. The rows should be `m|0` corrected to `|0` (i.e., `|m|0` style consistent with the last row: a leading `|` followed by the `m` cell marker). This makes the documented exit-code contract — which scripts depend on — visually broken in the published guide.
